name: Reputation update

subjectOf.text: Reputation update functions on each surface must be continuous in the validation pool's resolution outcome, because discontinuities in reputation update destroy continuity of best-response correspondences and preclude application of Brouwer's fixed-point theorem.
subjectOf.abstract: The reputation update functions on each surface are continuous in the validation pool's resolution outcome. Discontinuities in reputation update destroy continuity of best-response correspondences and preclude application of Brouwer.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Possibility Loops An Operational Architecture for Computative Economics in Agent Coordination Systems (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6655138
scope_conditions: architectures relying on Brouwer for equilibrium existence

subjectOf.text: The reputation update is an asymmetric multiplicative rule in which reputation is multiplied by one plus alpha when a vote matches the revealed key and by one minus gamma when it does not, with alpha fixed at 0.05, gamma at 0.10, and a floor applied after each update.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The parent paper requires only that gamma exceed alpha; this design fixes both rates.
Any single weight above one half is capped there and the excess redistributed among the other seated validators.
